transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's so very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for fitting me in. 

Well, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this, but... for the past year or so, I just feel like I'm always puttering around. You know, fixing little things, arranging the house, volunteering for just one more project. I always try to be helpful, which is a good thing, isn't it? But... well, even at 87, I just seem to have a terribly hard time just sitting down and being still. 

I feel a bit silly bringing it up, honestly, since staying active is supposed to be a positive thing at my age. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory or your ability to keep track of daily tasks lately?

Oh, goodness, no. No, my memory is still quite good, thankfully. I still manage all my own little errands and keep track of my schedule just fine. I suppose I write things down on my calendar just to be safe, which is the responsible thing to do, isn't it? But... well, I haven't missed any appointments or forgotten anything important. 

I wouldn't want you to worry that my mind is going! I'm still sharp as a tack, I promise. It really is just this... this silly restlessness I have, always needing to be up and doing something. I hope I'm answering your question properly?
When you feel this need to be constantly busy, do you also find yourself experiencing persistent feelings of worry or apprehension about various aspects of your life?

Oh, no, no... I wouldn't say that at all. I'm really quite a happy person, overall. I don't sit around fretting about things, if that's what you mean. 

I know some people my age worry terribly about their health or their families, but I always try to look on the bright side. It's so much better to just be positive, don't you think? So, no, it really isn't worry that keeps me moving... it's just that funny little urge to keep my hands busy and be of use. 

I hope that's a good thing? I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm an anxious sort of person. I hope I'm making sense!
When you feel this urge to keep moving, do you experience any uncomfortable sensations in your legs, such as tingling, pulling, or an irresistible need to move them to find relief?

Oh, my, no... nothing like that. No tingling or pulling or anything uncomfortable. My legs feel perfectly fine, I assure you. 

It's really not a physical discomfort at all. It's just... well, just me wanting to be up and doing things. I don't have to move my legs to make them feel better, I just... I just like to be active. 

I know some people get those awful aches and pains, but I've been very blessed in that regard. I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think there's something physically wrong with my nerves or anything like that. I'm really quite healthy for my age, I think!
When you feel this urge to keep moving, do you feel an internal sense of inner tension or pressure that is only relieved when you are actually doing something?

Oh, goodness, no. It's nothing like a pressure, really. That sounds so... well, so intense, doesn't it? I wouldn't say I feel tense at all. 

It's more just a little extra energy, you know? Like I just have a bit too much pep in my step sometimes. I don't feel forced to do things, I just... I just enjoy being busy. It's a good thing to be productive, right? 

I really don't feel any sort of uncomfortable tension building up inside me. I'm usually quite relaxed, actually, as long as I have a little project to tinker with. I hope that makes sense? I certainly don't want to sound like I'm wound up too tight or anything.
When you are not able to be busy or productive, do you feel a sense of guilt or that you are not being a 'good' or 'useful' person?

Oh, heavens, no. I wouldn't say I feel guilty. That sounds so terribly sad, doesn't it? To feel like you aren't a good person just because you're resting. No, I know I've done my fair share of hard work in my eighty-seven years! 

I just... well, I just prefer to be doing something. But if I have to sit still, like if I'm visiting with a friend or waiting at an appointment, I certainly don't beat myself up over it. I don't feel useless at all, I just try to be a pleasant companion instead. 

I hope that's the right way to look at it? I'd hate for you to think I have a poor opinion of myself or that I'm terribly hard on myself. I really do try to keep a healthy, balanced outlook on things, I promise.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical health, such as new medications, changes in your sleep patterns, or any recent medical diagnoses since this urge to stay busy began?

Oh, goodness me, no. I'm very happy to report that my health has been remarkably steady. I haven't had to start any new medications at all... well, just my usual daily vitamins, of course. And my sleep is just fine. I rest quite peacefully most nights. 

There haven't been any new medical problems or anything frightening like that. I try very hard to take excellent care of myself, you see. And really, this... this preference for staying active, it isn't exactly a sudden change. I've always been a bit of a busy bee, my whole life! 

I do hope that's alright? I'd hate for you to worry that my health was failing or that I wasn't looking after myself properly. I really am quite sturdy for eighty-seven, don't you think?
Has anyone in your life, such as a friend or family member, expressed concern or frustration that you are too busy or that you don't spend enough time just relaxing with them?

Oh, dear. Well... I suppose there might have been a tiny little incident at the senior center recently. It really wasn't a big fuss, just a small misunderstanding, I'm sure. 

I help out at the sign-up table, you see, and I suppose I was just moving things along a bit too briskly. I had to apologize to a few folks after one of our meetings. One of my dear friends gently suggested that maybe I should take a smaller role there. She felt my... well, my energetic manner was making things just a little tense for people who like to take their time. 

I felt just terrible about it, of course. I only ever want to be helpful and keep things running smoothly. I do hope you don't think I'm a difficult person to be around? I always try my very best to be considerate of everyone's feelings.
When you are at home by yourself, do you feel an internal pressure to keep finding tasks to do, or are you just as happy to sit and read a book or watch television for an entire afternoon?

Oh, heavens, no. I wouldn't say I feel any sort of... well, pressure. That sounds so terribly stressful, doesn't it? 

When I'm at home all by myself, I am perfectly delighted to just sit in my favorite chair with a nice cup of tea and read a book, or perhaps watch one of my programs on the television. I mean, I might pop up to water a plant if I notice it's dry, or putter about for a moment, but I certainly don't feel forced to scour the house for chores. I can relax for a whole afternoon just beautifully. 

I do hope that sounds like a sensible way to spend the day? I wouldn't want you to think I'm just running myself ragged behind closed doors. I really do know how to pace myself and enjoy a quiet afternoon, I promise.

Has this feedback from your friend about your energy level been a recurring theme in your life, or was that specific incident at the senior center the first time you've ever been told that your pace was making others uncomfortable?

Oh, my... well, I suppose if I'm being perfectly honest, it might not be the very first time. I do hope you won't think poorly of me, but... well, I've always been a rather spirited person. 

Even way back when I was just a little girl in grade school, I remember the teachers gently scolding me now and then. I'd pop out of my seat without thinking, or maybe I'd accidentally talk over the other children when I got too excited. They used to say I was just a bit 'too lively'—and that was long before I even became a teenager! 

But I always meant well, I truly did. I just had so much enthusiasm to share. I suppose that same lively spirit has just stayed with me all these years. It's not a terrible thing to be cheerful and energetic, is it? I always try my best to be polite, I just... sometimes I get a little carried away, I suppose.
